record.original_question: Characterize those Banach spaces in which every Chebyshev set is convex.

evidence.quote: the following problem arises naturally : Characterize those Banach spaces in which every Cebysev set is convex.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X, \|\cdot\|)$ be a real Banach space. A nonempty subset $C \subseteq X$ is called a Chebyshev set if for every $x \in X$ there exists a unique point $p_C(x) \in C$ such that
$$\|x - p_C(x)\| = \inf_{y \in C} \|x - y\|.$$
A subset $C \subseteq X$ is convex if $\lambda y + (1-\lambda) z \in C$ whenever $y, z \in C$ and $\lambda \in [0,1]$.

Provide an intrinsic characterization of those real Banach spaces $X$ with the property that every Chebyshev subset of $X$ is convex. That is, find necessary and sufficient conditions on the Banach space $X$ under which the implication "$C \subseteq X$ is a Chebyshev set $\Rightarrow$ $C$ is convex" holds for every nonempty $C \subseteq X$.
artifact.status_search_result: The convexity of Chebyshev sets remains a major unsolved problem in approximation theory. Even the special case of whether every Chebyshev subset of an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space must be convex is famously open. Numerous sufficient conditions (e.g., continuity or non-expansiveness of the metric projection, weak closedness, approximate compactness) are known, but a full intrinsic characterization of Banach spaces in which every Chebyshev set is convex has not been obtained.

status_evidence.claim: The convexity of Chebyshev sets in Hilbert space (a special case) is explicitly noted as an unsolved problem.

status_evidence.claim: The general problem of convexity of Chebyshev sets in Banach/normed spaces is the subject of survey work and remains open.
